symbols.name: input array
symbols.meaning: The logical array on input wire 1 of the gate.
symbols.quote: Let $g_1, g_2, \dots, g_t$ be the logical arrays on the $t$ input wires of the gate, so $g_s$ is the logical array on input wire $s$.

symbols.name: second input array
symbols.meaning: The logical array on input wire 2 of the gate.
symbols.quote: Let $g_1, g_2, \dots, g_t$ be the logical arrays on the $t$ input wires of the gate, so $g_s$ is the logical array on input wire $s$.

symbols.name: last input array
symbols.meaning: The logical array on the last of the $t$ input wires of the gate.
symbols.quote: Let $g_1, g_2, \dots, g_t$ be the logical arrays on the $t$ input wires of the gate, so $g_s$ is the logical array on input wire $s$.

symbols.name: other frame
symbols.meaning: An invertible operator on arrays that one incidence uses in place of the gate's frame $D_v$.
symbols.quote: Suppose the second incidence used a different invertible operator $D'$ in place of $D_v$, with nonzero weights $\alpha_1,\alpha_2$.

symbols.name: moving-back operator
symbols.meaning: The single operator that would move the gate's result back to logical form.
symbols.quote: while one operator $\Gamma$ would have to move the result back to logical form, giving $\Gamma(\alpha_1 g_1+\alpha_2 g_2)$.

relations.quote: An incidence relates a wire to a [Gate and terminal of a network](network-gate-terminal.md): it holds when the wire touches that gate or terminal.
Every incidence lies in a linear network, and the [frame of a gate](linear-network-frames.md) is shared by all its incidences.
